summary.name: VimR
summary.one_liner: VimR is a macOS graphical front end for Neovim, written in Swift, that embeds Neovim with GUI conveniences.
use_cases: Editing code or text in a native macOS window with Neovim
Previewing Markdown or HTML files while editing
Quickly opening files with a fuzzy finder
Embedding Neovim in a Cocoa app via the NvimView package
Building and installing a local VimR release from source
summary.what_it_does: VimR is a Neovim GUI for macOS written in Swift, built to run Neovim inside a native editor window with some GUI features found in other editors. It includes Markdown and generic HTML preview (the HTML preview keeps scroll position on reload), a fuzzy file finder similar to Xcode's Open Quickly, a simple file browser, and a command line tool. Trackpad pinch-to-zoom and two-finger scrolling are supported, and ligatures are available but off by default. The project is split into reusable Swift packages (NvimView, NvimApi, Commons, Tabs, Workspace, Ignore) that can be used independently.
notable: Modular Swift packages such as NvimView that embed Neovim in a Cocoa app
Pre-built universal signed and notarized binaries under Releases
Flexible workspace model similar to JetBrains IDEs
caveats: Building from source requires Xcode 26 and Homebrew dependencies
